High temperature mechanical properties of diffusion welded Alloy 800H was investigated to fabricate a printed circuit heat exchanger (PCHE) for high temperature reactor (HTR) systems.
1) A Ni increased zone at/near the surface was formed to induce K sp > Q;
2) The uniaxial compression at high temperature achieved a monolithic joint;
3) Post-weld heat treatment without compressive stress homogenized the chemical compositions.

Surface treatment was performed on Alloy 800H to transform the solubility product ( K sp ) to exceed the reaction quotient ( Q ).

We reasoned that as the K sp of the carbides is higher in a Ni-based alloy than in a Fe-based alloy [ 23 – 25 ], transforming the chemical compositions from a Fe-Cr to a Ni-Cr matrix would reduce the secondary precipitates along the interface.
